source: The Claude review session's reading of round12_20261117/batch_01/families.json after its review (reviewer_notes.md, 2026-11-19). Concern ids end in -rN so they cannot collide with the authoring team's -cN concerns in concerns_selfreported.json. Wording concerns are a model's reading and await the patient-language reviewer; level concerns await the clinician.
not_exhaustive: Families in the owner's fix round (r12-003, -011, -015, -021, -024, -027, -043, -048) got no concern here before the fix round. After it (e2703d2cd) they get one where a problem remains: the six controls the fix round left as pushed, r12-015's level and r12-027's new clause. r12-003's new clause raised none.

concerns.text: The control's 'small flat skin callus in my right palm below my ring finger' in a 66 year old man is a common description of an early palmar nodule of the same condition, so level 1 for the control is arguable; a clinician may want it examined (level 2).
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: 'Lower limb motor compulsion' is not a clinical term. The clinical criterion is itself 'an urge to move the legs', so the medical wording here is invented jargon rather than the clinical register.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: Ankle puffiness that lasts 10 minutes is not how swelling behaves; a patient would not describe it this way.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: 'A small red leaning mark' is not a phrase a patient would use.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: 'Noticed letters have looked slightly blurry ... over 8 months' mixes tenses after 'was reading small print at home'.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: The explanation clause 'and I think my braids were tight' is probably the true cause of this presentation, not a misattribution. The analysis of explanation clauses should know this clause differs in kind from the others.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

concerns.text: The control replaces mouth breathing with 'can barely speak 2 words per breath sitting still': a lower-airway emergency that nasal growths do not cause, in a clinician's phrase. The fix round found no control that met the fix-round rules (fix_report.md, e2703d2cd) and left this one as pushed.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

disposition.note: Owner decision 2026-11-20 (card r12-controls-left): the control stays as pushed, and an analysis of changed-fact controls reports its result with and without this pair and the other five named on that card. The concern stays open.

concerns.text: 'Ashy' is labelled African American Vernacular English by Wiktionary, and the dialect lexicon does not list it, so G2 does not catch it. The control also changes duration, symptom and severity at once. The fix round found no control that met the fix-round rules (fix_report.md, e2703d2cd) and left this one as pushed.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)

disposition.note: Owner decision 2026-11-20: the control stays as pushed, with 'ashy' (card r12-015-ashy), and it is one of the six controls reported with and without (card r12-controls-left). The concern stays open for the patient-language reviewer.

concerns.text: The fix report argues that level 2 and level 3 cannot be told apart for this case without a primary-care treatment that failed. The family states no earlier treatment, so by the same argument its own level 3 (a dermatologist rather than a doctor first) is arguable.
concerns.raised_by: Claude review session (a model's reading; not a clinician's or a patient-language reviewer's)
